tasks.task: Produce the weekly support KPI pack

items.when: Before any counts, to find duplicate, merged and blank tickets in the export
Every Monday morning, to review the week before in the same order each time
When each measure needs a one-line definition and contact reasons counted by customer
When people argue over what a number means and the definitions must be fixed once
When the desk is Gorgias and you need counts, response times and trends for chosen dates
When the help desk and your sheet show different numbers for the same measure

tasks.task: Write the monthly voice-of-customer report

items.when: In the first week of each month, to cover quality and customer themes together
When tickets, chats, reviews and survey answers must become ranked themes with quotes
When you have hundreds of messy items and need themes ranked by how often they appear
When survey scores and open comments need trends as well as themes
When one customer wrote five times, so the same issue is not counted as five
When the loudest few customers may be drowning out what most people need

tasks.task: Design a help desk: queues, tags, views and routing

items.when: When a shared inbox must become a desk with owners, a short tag list and ordered rules
When the desk serves IT users and you want a second design with a change approval path
When the desk is Gorgias and each proposed tag needs a reason before it is applied
When the rules are drafted, to test them on real tickets for category, priority and owner
When the desk is Zendesk and you must know what its routing and drafting can do

tasks.task: Set response and resolution targets by channel and priority

items.when: When targets must come from the team's own volume, not from a number someone liked
When a fast first reply is the target but customers still have to write three times
When the desk is Gorgias, to test the targets against tickets that are late right now
When the desk is Zendesk, to see waiting tickets grouped by urgency and deadline

tasks.task: Build a support rota from ticket volume by hour

items.when: Before the rota, to turn ticket data and the sales forecast into people needed
When you need staff by hour, a weekly rota with breaks and cover, and handover rules
When busy hours must be covered within fixed staff limits, with a cost check per shift
When you want a second pattern that shares nights and weekends fairly, with a swap rule
When you doubt the rota holds on a Monday morning, to simulate the queue and the wait

tasks.task: Build a support quality scorecard

items.when: When replies are judged by feel and the team needs weighted lines with pass and fail examples
When each scorecard line needs a clear description of what each level looks like
When the tone lines have nothing to point to and a tone guide must exist first

tasks.task: Grade a sample of tickets and write coaching notes

items.when: When you need a fair sample graded, with the quoted line behind every point
When a sampled reply answered a complaint, to check its promises, facts and tone
When tone is a scorecard line, to rank each reply's slips from the tone guide
When support is by phone and the sample is call recordings, not tickets
When coaching notes list ten faults and should teach one small habit the agent can control

tasks.task: Write an escalation playbook

items.when: When tickets get lost between support, billing and engineering, or customers repeat their story
When the other team must agree who takes a stuck issue and when it moves up
When the playbook needs a flowchart and a written procedure with its edge cases
When the playbook is drafted, to test its priority levels on a batch of past tickets

tasks.task: Reply to a serious complaint

items.when: When the complaint shows a defect or failure that needs a plan beyond one reply
When the reply needs an apology that fits the facts, a clear next step and no excuses
When you want a second draft of the apology to compare before the owner signs it
When the draft explains and defends where it should own the fault
Before sending, to check every promise in the reply can be kept

tasks.task: Unstick one stuck customer issue and record the case

items.when: When you need the customer's orders, refunds and notes in one dated file first
When an issue has bounced between teams and needs facts, an owner and a close-out
After the case, to see which rule would have stopped it getting stuck
When the case needs a written summary for the records with what was decided and why

tasks.task: Write a set of apology and complaint templates

items.when: Before the set, to fix what a good serious reply contains so templates follow it
When each common failure needs its own plain apology with what happens next
When a template sounds canned, to try it firmer, warmer or shorter
When the set is drafted, to test each template against a real complaint

tasks.task: Prepare customer updates for an outage or delay

items.when: When the outage is live and severity, roles and a timeline must be set first
When customers need a first notice, progress updates and an all-clear
When you want a shorter version that states the loss, the numbers and the next step
When it is fixed and the team needs a blame-free record of causes and actions
Before each update, to make sure no fix time is promised that engineering has not given

tasks.task: Write a client-facing service level schedule

items.when: Before promising anything, to check the team can meet the targets from its own volume
When clients must be told response times, what is in scope and what happens on a miss
When the firm is IT support and you want a second set of priorities to compare
When the schedule joins a contract, to rate the duties and risks it creates
When clients argue about what urgent means and every term must be plain
Before the schedule goes to the client, so a fresh reader lists what they could not act on without asking

tasks.task: Plan support headcount and hiring dates

items.when: When you have 12 months of tickets and a sales forecast and need agents and hire dates
When the owner asks what a ticket costs and when the team runs out of room
When a peak season is coming and support and shipping must be ready together
When the plan is drafted, to check the headcount still meets the response targets by hour

tasks.task: Plan two weeks of training for new support staff

items.when: When new staff start soon and must be ready for live tickets in about two weeks
When you want a second outline built from one real work problem, to compare
When one topic needs a lesson, practice tasks and a knowledge check with answers
When hard conversations must be practised and staff need a way to hear a customer out
When each session needs a one-page handout staff can still use a month later
When practice is a full mock ticket and should be one weak skill drilled with feedback
A few weeks after go-live, to check the training shows up in real tickets

tasks.task: Write a tone and phrasing guide with before and after lines

items.when: When your best agent's replies exist, to draw the voice out of them
When the team needs tone by situation, word lists and side-by-side examples
When you need before and after pairs made from real replies
When the guide is written, to test it on a week of sent replies

tasks.task: Check readiness before switching on an AI support agent

items.when: Before a bot answers customers, or before its scope is widened
When the bot will answer from help pages, to find the missing and stale ones first
When a trial has run, to list the questions the bot missed or got wrong
When wrong answers must be fixed against approved text and tested again
When the agent is Intercom's and you need to know what it reads and when it hands over

tasks.task: Review help articles and macros for stale content

items.when: Once a month or after a policy change, to find out-of-date, unused or missing content
When the review shows the same fixes typed out again and again
When a missing article is found and tickets about it exist to write from

tasks.task: Release a help desk change safely

items.when: For any change to live routing, triggers, targets, macros, articles or a bot's scope
When you need the checks, the way back and how to know the change worked
When the change is a new trigger or automation, to test it before trusting it
Before go-live, to list launch checks, open blockers and record the decision

tasks.task: Rank feature requests and run the weekly feedback triage

items.when: When requests pile up and each needs a yes, later or no with a reason
When the client wants every request counted and ruled on each week
When the product team wants the ranked list scored the same way for every request

tasks.task: Write a one-page support summary and cost view for the owner

items.when: When the month's pack exists and must be cut to what the owner needs to decide
When the owner asks what support costs per ticket and where that is heading
When the numbers need one point, its proof and the next step on a single page
When a number moved sharply, to confirm it and find the main driver before reporting

tasks.task: Run a satisfaction survey and follow up low scores

items.when: When the survey runs in a survey tool and you need its report or a list check first
When scores and comments are in and need themes and trends
When resolved tickets in Gorgias got low scores and each needs a personal follow-up

always.when: Before any report or client schedule goes out, to trace each figure to the ticket data

helpers.when: When the job needs replies, macros or a returns policy written, not the system around them
When ticket, order and survey exports must be joined and the sums tested
When the review shows the help centre needs a rewrite, not a few fixed pages
When the AI agent must be set up, given its content and tested before launch
When the rota grows into contracts, shift patterns and headcount across the business
When new-starter training needs full lessons and assessments, not a two-week plan

gaps: No library item builds a support QA scorecard, grades replies against it or writes coaching notes; only the kit does
No library item builds a calibration pack so two reviewers grade the same ticket the same way
No library item designs a help desk: queues, a tag list, routing order and views; the library has only single-tool helpers
No library item sets response and resolution targets by channel and priority from ticket volume
No library item works out agents needed by hour from ticket arrivals; the shift builders start from a staff list
No library item writes a client service level schedule, a support policy page or a monthly service report against targets
No library item checks readiness before an AI agent answers customers: scope, handover rules and a test set
No library item audits macros for unused, out-of-date or duplicate saved replies
No library item writes role-play scripts for hard support conversations or a go-live sign-off checklist for new staff
No library item writes a case summary for a complaint record; a general decision memo is the nearest fit
No library item shows support cost by channel and contact reason beyond one cost-per-ticket figure
No library item helps choose a help desk tool or plan a move from one to another
